title: The orbit category ]X/G[ as a Lean category
body_html:
The orbit category $\,]X/G[\,$

Following Sheaf7 §2.7 (the definitions surrounding lem:qfd_equiv).

The orbit category $]X/G[$ has:

  • objects: cells of $X$;
  • morphisms $E \to E'$: elements $g \in G$ such that $g\cdot E \preceq E'$ (equivalently, $g\cdot E$ is a face of $E'$);
  • composition: for $\alpha = g_1 : E \to E'$ and $\beta = g_2 : E' \to E''$, the composite is $g_2 g_1 : E \to E''$; well-typed because $(g_2 g_1)\cdot E = g_2\cdot(g_1\cdot E) \preceq g_2\cdot E' \preceq E''$ using cellularity of the $G$-action (Cellular G-action on an abstract cell complex);
  • identity: $\mathbf 1 : E \to E$ from $\mathbf 1\cdot E = E \preceq E$.

The opposite category $[X/G] := ]X/G[^{\mathrm{op}}$ is the more common target — every "orbit-category" statement in the paper is written for $[X/G]$ (matching the cosheaf convention).

Lean formalization

The Lean file uses an abbrev-alias for the type

abbrev OrbitCat (G X : Type*) : Type _ := X

so that the MulAction G X/PartialOrder X/AbstractCellComplex X instances remain visible without manual transfer. Morphisms are packaged as a Subtype

def Mor (E E' : OrbitCat G X) : Type _ :=
  {g : G // g • (E : X) ≤ (E' : X)}

(rather than a fresh structure) so that the universe of Mor E E' matches the universe of G, keeping the Category typeclass happy. The Category (OrbitCat G X) instance is declared scoped — activated only inside open OrbitCat — so that it does not shadow X's Preorder-derived category structure used by Sheaves and cosheaves on X as functor categories.

The face-relation composition ((g_2 g_1)\cdot E \preceq E'') follows from GCellComplex.smul_le and transitivity of ≤, wrapped as Mor.comp. The three Category axioms (id_comp, comp_id, assoc) collapse to the corresponding facts about group multiplication, wrapped in Subtype.ext.
